accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Edexcel and OCR A level Mathematics specifications (statistical hypothesis testing: understand and apply the language of hypothesis testing, including test statistic; conduct a test for the proportion of a binomial distribution) and a standard A level statistics text on binomial tests. Every number was recomputed: the lab's P(X = k) uses the exact recurrence P(k+1) = P(k)(n − k)p/((k + 1)(1 − p)); for B(20, 0.5), P(X ≥ 13) = 0.1316, P(X ≥ 15) = 0.0207 and P(X ≥ 17) = 0.0013 (verified with exact sums in Python), so 15 and 17 fall under 5% and 13 does not. Sample proportions 15/60 = 1/4, 14/20 = 0.7, 21/30 = 0.7 and 9/40 = 0.225 were checked; means np and variances np(1 − p) in the items hold at every parameter corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors: giving the parameter p or the number of trials as the test statistic (step 1 options and feedback, challenge), using the sample proportion in B(n, p) (step 2 prediction and the 1/4, 0.7 chips; challenge B(40, 0.225)), swapping the observed count and n (the n = 15 chip; challenge B(9, 0.3)), believing H₀ is assumed because it is true (challenge), thinking the data change the null distribution (step 5 prediction), forcing a binomial onto a waiting time or sampling without replacement (step 4), and reading a tail probability as the probability H₀ is true (mastery m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtstat is about the test statistic and its sampling distribution under H₀: choosing the count X for four contexts, assembling X ~ B(n, p₀) from n and p chips with the distribution drawn from exact binomial probabilities, a coin simulation whose dark bars converge on the pale B(20, 0.5) bars, a binomial-conditions sort, a p₀ slider that moves the distribution while the observed 14 stays fixed, and a draggable marker that shades P(X ≥ x). lab_distinct kept it under 30% against flagnullh, flagbinp, flagbshape, flagbcrit and every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The ideas come from the learner's actions: tapping p = 1/4 returns '1/4 is the sample proportion. The null distribution assumes H₀, so p = 1/6'; running the simulation makes the null distribution appear from H₀ alone; dragging the slider shows the bars move while the red data line does not; dragging the marker to 15 shows P(X ≥ 15) = 2.1% and the learner then judges it unusual under H₀.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions hold a tempting wrong answer that the step disproves: the sample proportion 1/4 as p (the build step rejects it), most simulated counts landing near the observed 15 (the simulation piles up at 10), and the data setting the null distribution (the slider step moves H₀ with the data fixed). The done line repeats the learner's prediction against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: sample proportion in place of p₀, observed count in place of n, parameter as statistic, significance level as statistic, H₀ believed true, sample proportion thought unknown, fairness confused with fixed n, constant p blamed instead of fixed n, data thought to change, n thought to depend on H₀, observed count as the mean, and p as the mean. Step 1 has four distinct messages (parameter, trials, single trial, waiting time).

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs explain one idea each with a worked example (For 60 rolls of a dice with H₀: p = 1/6, it is X ~ B(60, 1/6)) and pass the readability limit for this age; the adult text uses the precise terms test statistic, null distribution, sampling distribution, parameter, p₀, independence and constant p and names the mark-scheme requirement to define X in context.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stays under the 12% six-word overlap limit against every lesson, including Null and alternative hypotheses, Binomial probabilities and When a binomial model fits. Every hint names the step to take (np, np(1 − p), which number comes from H₀).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark for every step and after wrong taps: the step-1 options were moved up after feedback overlapped the last option, the build step's X ~ B(?, ?) line and last-built histogram were moved below the chip grid after overlapping it, and every subtitle was moved below the title pill. Histogram tick labels use the theme text colour, and the slider knob is 28 px across.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a button: each statistic option, Choose n = 60, Run 10 more, Run 100 more, the binomial sort boxes, p − 0.05 and p + 0.05 for the slider, ◀ and ▶ for the marker, and Common or Unusual if H₀ is true. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line.
